title: Wire search/seller executors into @loxep/app
description:
Phase 2 primitives for search rules, seller monitoring, and new-listing detection are implemented and tested in @loxep/integration-ebay and @loxep/market (loxep-7dp.1/.2), but NOTHING calls them: the poll executor in @loxep/app has no branch for the new target types. This issue is the wiring.

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY (do not rebuild):
- @loxep/integration-ebay: searchListings(adapter, {query?, categoryId?, filters?, sort?, limit?, cursor?}) and searchAllListings(adapter, {..., maxItems}) over Browse search; fetchSellerListings/fetchAllSellerListings(adapter, {sellerUsername, query?, categoryId?, filters?, sort?, limit?, cursor?, maxItems}) over the Browse 'sellers' filter. Both return normalized EbayListingSummary values plus total/offset/limit/cursor/warnings. Application token only (EbayAdapter, never EbayUserAdapter).
- @loxep/market: monitorTargetConfigSchemas.ebay_search / .ebay_seller; diffDiscoveredItems({knownExternalIds, fetchedSummaries}); knownExternalItemIds(db, {provider, marketplace, externalItemIds}); deriveNewListingEvents(db, {monitorTargetId, newlyLinkedItems, detectedAt?}).

WHAT THE EXECUTOR BRANCH MUST DO (per claimed target, target_type in ('ebay_search','ebay_seller')):
1. Mint ONE observationBatchId and fix observedAt at fetch time; both must survive retries (the observation write path keys on them).
2. Build the adapter from the target's connection; pass the connection's shared RateBudget. maxItems (config, default e.g. 200) bounds paging - each page spends budget.
3. ebay_search: searchAllListings(adapter, {query, categoryId, filters, sort: 'newlyListed', maxItems}). ebay_seller: fetchAllSellerListings(adapter, {sellerUsername, query, categoryId, filters, maxItems}). config.filters.listedAfter is an ISO STRING in jsonb; the adapter accepts Date|string, so it can be passed through unchanged.
4. BEFORE upserting anything, call knownExternalItemIds(db, {provider:'ebay', marketplace: adapter.marketplaceId, externalItemIds}) and diffDiscoveredItems(...). After the upsert every item looks known, so the order is load-bearing.
5. For every fetched summary: upsertMarketplaceItem (summary fields map 1:1 - externalItemId, title, price/currency, canonicalUrl, sellerExternalId, conditionCode, categoryExternalId, listingType, listingStartedAt, listingEndsAt) then linkItemToMonitor(db, {monitorTargetId, marketplaceItemId, at: observedAt}).
6. Record an observation batch for the page (search summaries carry no quantity/availability - leave those NULL, never 0).
7. Call deriveNewListingEvents(db, {monitorTargetId, newlyLinkedItems: <the diff's newItems, mapped to marketplaceItemId + payload facts>, detectedAt}) AFTER linking. It is idempotent and only fires on first GLOBAL discovery.
8. Report recordPollSuccess with changed = (newItems.length > 0 || any derived event), plus the rate-budget floor as bounds.minSeconds.
9. Inspect page.warnings: errorId 12002 means eBay IGNORED a filter and returned unfiltered results, 12008 means it ignored the sort. Log them; treat 12002 on a monitor as a configuration error rather than as discovery data. fetchSellerListings already THROWS on 12003 (unknown seller) rather than returning the anchor's whole result set.

GOTCHAS VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE SANDBOX (2026-08-11):
- eBay rejects a filter-only search with errorId 12001; a seller filter is NOT an anchor. Seller enumeration therefore defaults to EBAY_ROOT_CATEGORY_ID ('0'), which is undocumented but observed to work when paired with a valid seller filter.
- limit max 200; an invalid sort is only a warning, so the local sort enum is the real guard.
- Browse only returns currently purchasable listings, so an item missing from a page is NOT evidence the listing ended. Do not derive listing_ended from absence.

TESTS TO ADD WITH THE WIRING: an executor-level test that a second poll of the same search discovers nothing new and derives no second new_listing, and one that two overlapping monitors over the same item produce exactly one new_listing.

Commerce schema migrations and order ingestion services shipped, PROVISIONALLY, per an explicit owner directive: every open question in commerce-schema-design.md is resolved per its own documented recommendation, implemented, and marked PROVISIONAL for review.

SCHEMA (packages/db/src/schema/commerce.ts + migrations/0003_commerce_orders_and_catalog.sql, hand-reviewed): the design's ten tables — orders, order_lines, order_fees, order_refunds, order_refund_lines, order_fulfillments, order_fulfillment_lines, order_source_links, catalog_items, channel_listings. NO existing table gains a column, exactly as the design targets. Conventions held: uuid PKs, timestamptz, numeric(20,6) money, text state columns with TS unions and no PG enums, CHECK only for Loxep-owned closed sets (entity_attribution_source, fee_scope, fee_direction, catalog kind, source-link effect + num_nonnulls), ADR-0020 nullable SET NULL user FKs on orders.entity_attributed_by_user_id and catalog_items.created_by_user_id only, no jsonb payload/attribute bag anywhere, no hypertable. Verified live against drizzle-kit 0.31.10 / pg18: UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT, partial unique indexes, and num_nonnulls all emit correctly — no constraint had to be weakened. db suite migrates from zero, MIGRATION_FILE_COUNT 3 -> 4, green.

SCHEMA DELTAS vs the draft: (1) order_fees gains fee_direction text not null CHECK ('seller_charge'|'buyer_surcharge') — NOT in the draft, forced by the Woo finding that fee_lines are buyer surcharges already inside orders.total while Woo core reports no seller-side fees at all. Inverting signs would silently corrupt every fee report; dropping the rows would lose a real fact. orders.fee_amount stays a seller-side magnitude (0 for Woo) and profitability subtracts only seller_charge. (2) fulfillment_status unions gain 'unknown' (Woo's 'refunded' erases prior fulfillment knowledge). (3) order_fulfillments.status gets an explicit union the draft only named. (4) fee_type gains 'buyer_surcharge'. (5) subtotal_amount stays not-null and DERIVED (exact scaled-integer sum at the adapter), not nullable.

INGESTION (@loxep/commerce): a provider-NEUTRAL CommerceOrderFact is the only shape that reaches the database; wooOrderFactToCommerceFact translates WooOrderFact at the boundary (ADR-0009), so eBay/Medusa are a translator plus a status table, not a second ingestion service. createOrderIngestionService({db}).ingestWooOrder/{ingestOrderFact} upserts on (connection_id, provider, external_order_id) in ONE transaction. order_lines are matched IN PLACE by stable external line identity (positional fallback), with survivors parked in negative line-number space so a provider that renumbers cannot collide with unique(order_id, line_number) mid-rewrite — preserving line ids that order_refund_lines and order_fulfillment_lines reference. Fees/refunds/fulfillments are delete-and-replaced in the same transaction, the strategy the design prescribes, so a reversed refund actually disappears. Provenance: the raw payload lands in provider_objects (one row per distinct payload hash — an unchanged re-sync reuses it) and is linked through order_source_links with effect created/updated/unchanged. Cross-connection duplicates are auto-linked via duplicate_of_order_id with NO unique constraint (detect, don't constrain).

SYNC + SCHEDULING (design open question 6): reuses monitor_targets with target type 'woo_orders' and the cursor under a namespaced config.commerceSync key — no second scheduler, no commerce_sync_cursors table, no new column. Watermark is the last date_modified_gmt SEEN (Woo's modified_after is EXCLUSIVE) rewound one second so a same-second tie across a page boundary is re-read rather than lost. @loxep/market exposes NO target-type registration seam (closed z.enum + closed config record), so @loxep/commerce owns wooOrdersTargetConfigSchema and writes the row with a direct insert, taking no market dependency; claimDueTargets/recordPollSuccess/recordPollFailure are already type-agnostic, so the row is claimable the moment an app-side executor knows it. jobs task commerce.sync-woo-orders with a dependency-injected adapter factory and jobKey per connection; createCommerceTasks returns a plain task list for @loxep/app to register.

TESTS: 46 in packages/commerce against real PostgreSQL — idempotence (same fact twice -> no dupes, one provenance link; changed fact -> updated, second link), stable line identity across a drop-and-renumber, the full attribution precedence matrix incl. immutability and the manual-never-rewritten rule, fee direction and scope, refund + refund-line mapping and removal, fulfillment per-line quantities, Woo 'refunded' and unrecognized-plugin-status -> 'unknown', duplicate detection across two connections, catalog SKU uniqueness, channel link suggestions, hand-computed profitability, exact decimal arithmetic, and the sync/cursor path through the REAL adapter with only fetch stubbed. LIVE tier against the production store (read-only, GETs only, 2 pages of 5): 10 orders / 10 lines / 5 fulfillments / 10 provenance links / 0 fees, currency [USD], subtotal+shipping+tax reconciled exactly to gross, no buyer PII in any domain column, and an immediate re-run created 0.

GATES: db + commerce + domain + market + notifications suites green; every package typechecks; node import gate on @loxep/commerce and the new schema passes; docs build green (42 pages, all internal links valid).

DOCS: commerce-schema-design.md gained a 'Provisional implementation decisions' section (what shipped, all eight questions as implemented, the deltas, and a ranked list of what a reviewer should push back on first) and its 'design work only' banner is corrected; domain-boundaries.md gained a PROVISIONAL 'Scheduling is shared foundation infrastructure' subsection with the three rules that keep it from becoming a dumping ground; foundation-schema.md points at the commerce extension and records the woo_orders target type.

Phase 4 inventory/acquisition/fulfillment schema design doc landed at apps/docs/src/content/docs/architecture/inventory-schema-design.md (975 lines), mirroring commerce-schema-design.md structure and rigor: scope, explicit non-goals, inherited conventions, entity attribution, cost-basis argument, per-table sketches with constraints, relationship overview, migration sketch with ordering/no-column-changes/index strategy, 10 open questions with recommendations, 7 documentation tensions, and an implementation checklist. Sidebar entry added in apps/docs/astro.config.mjs (Architecture, after Commerce Schema Design); roadmap Phase 4 gained a pointer line. bun run docs:build green, all internal links valid (41 pages). Nine designed tables: acquisitions, acquisition_costs, inventory_locations, inventory_items, inventory_allocations, inventory_movements, shipments, shipment_items, acquisition_opportunity_links. No existing table gains a column.

Load-bearing recommendations: (1) SPECIFIC IDENTIFICATION over FIFO for one-of-a-kind resale goods -- argued on non-fungibility, information already present at pick time, self-contradiction of per-item margin under an assumed cost flow, and decisively on reversibility (specific data can be re-reported as FIFO; FIFO data can never be re-reported specifically). No cost-layer table: an inventory_items row IS a layer, so FIFO is a picker policy (oldest acquired_at) selected by what the allocation identifies -- the exit path costs no migration. (2) Cost basis freezes at first depletion_sale; re-allocating an open lot redistributes only the unlocked remainder. (3) Entity attribution stored on BOTH acquisitions and inventory_items and IMMUTABLE; a change of owning entity is a paired transfer_out/transfer_in creating a new row, not an UPDATE -- preserving the Phase 3 write-once invariant while supporting personal-to-LLC contribution. (4) Movements are append-only with signed quantity and ONE location per row (a transfer is two rows sharing transfer_group_id), so on-hand and per-location balance stay a plain sum(); idempotency via deduplication_key reusing the market_events mechanism. (5) Allocation is NOT a movement -- reservations are intentions that may never happen.

OPEN QUESTIONS (10, each with a recommendation): 1 where a per-SKU costing policy would live (rec: none now; catalog_items.costing_method additively later, and that is Phase 3's document to amend, not this one). 2 append-only enforcement on inventory_movements (rec: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger; a TypeScript-only rule is a convention, not an invariant). 3 cache quantity_on_hand vs derive from movements (rec: cache with nightly reconciliation; deriving is on every availability path while the ledger only grows). 4 location on the item row vs a per-location balance table (rec: single column, split-on-transfer; the balance table is additive). 5 when cost basis freezes (rec: first depletion; never-locking lets a March re-allocation rewrite February margin). 6 which record is authoritative for marketplace-purchased postage (rec: shipments authoritative, order_fees stays as ingested evidence, shipments.order_fee_id links them so the read model excludes the fee -- without this every per-item margin subtracts postage twice). 7 pro-rata basis for allocating order-scoped fees and shipping to lines, closing Phase 3 open question 1 (rec: by line_total net of line discounts, largest-remainder rounding, computed never stored). 8 mixed currency between cost basis and sale (rec: no conversion in Phase 4, consistent with Phase 3; report the gap honestly rather than store a rate). 9 consignment goods (rec: ordinary items with zero basis, excluded from profitability by explicit predicate not by the accident of a zero; an ownership column is where this ends up). 10 non-capitalized acquisition costs before Phase 5 exists (rec: keep them; the risk is a labeling problem, not a schema one).

TENSIONS REPORTED, NOT FIXED (7): Phase 4's 'Marketplace/payment fees' roadmap bullet is now empty given the Phase 3/Phase 5 fee split; 'Purchasing/vendors/receiving foundation' in Phase 4 conflicts with Purchasing as a separate domain and vendors as DESIGN-FOR; three condition vocabularies exist and catalog_items.condition_code has now MIGRATED as nullable text with no CHECK despite condition being a property of a unit, not a SKU; shipping package ownership (@loxep/inventory vs @loxep/shipping) is undecided and has the same 'decide before implementation' shape as Phase 3's monitor_targets question; inventory valuation is scheduled in no phase; the domain map's 'FIFO, weighted-average, and specific-identification' DESIGN-FOR bullet would lead an implementer to build the cost-layer table this design argues against; and the opportunity-to-outcome correlation STUDY is unscheduled while Phase 4 delivers only the linkage table.

Also caught during finalization: the concurrently-applied Phase 3 migration added order_fees.fee_direction (seller_charge | buyer_surcharge), which the Phase 3 design document does not contain. The profitability composition was corrected to deduct only seller_charge rows -- subtracting a buyer surcharge understates contribution by an amount the buyer already paid. DOCS-ONLY; nothing committed.

ATTRIBUTION: orders.economic_entity_id is a STORED snapshot written ONCE at first normalization, never a read-time join through connections — re-attributing a connection cannot retroactively rewrite already-reported history. Precedence implemented and tested as a matrix: explicit per-order override -> 'manual'; else connections.economic_entity_id -> 'connection_default'; else null -> 'unattributed'. entity_attribution_source carries a CHECK (Loxep-owned closed set) and is the re-attribution eligibility marker. Failed-verification path: tampered source object -> copy fails sha256 verify -> bad destination copy removed, object row failed with mismatch error recorded, verifiedAt null, NO cutover (media row still on source), migration completed_with_errors, cleanup skips it.
